title: A dense open scheme in a relatively quasi-separated algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Y$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose the representable diagonal $Y\to Y\times_S Y$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests: its pullback along every scheme mapping to $Y\times_S Y$ is a quasi-compact morphism of schemes, meaning that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Then there exist a scheme $V$ over $S$ and an open immersion $j:V\to Y$ such that $|j|$ identifies $|V|$ homeomorphically with an open dense subset of $|Y|$. Here open immersion means a representable morphism whose pullback to every scheme is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and dense means that the closure is all of $|Y|$. No quasi-compactness, finite-type, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed. The empty space is allowed.

source.place: Tag 086U, theorem-decent-open-dense-scheme, with Tag 03JX, lemma-bounded-fibres, and definition-very-reasonable: quasi-separated spaces are decent. Relative quasi-separatedness over a scheme is reduced over affine open subsets of the base to this absolute condition; take the union of the resulting open schematic loci.

proof.text: Let $V=Y_{\mathrm{sch}}$ be the largest schematic open given by [lem-sfb-space-largest-schematic-open]. It suffices to show that every nonempty open subset $O\subseteq|Y|$ meets $|V|$. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] the open $O$ is an open subspace $Y_O$. Apply [lem-a1-space-affine-atlas-open-cover] to $Y_O$ and choose a nonempty member $X$ with affine surjective etale atlas $a:U\to X$ whose composite to $S$ factors through an affine open $B\subseteq S$. Thus $U$ is nonempty, $X$ is open in $Y$, and $X\to B$ is defined.

Put $R=U\times_XU$. The map $R\to U\times_BU$ is the pullback of the relative diagonal $\Delta_{Y/S}$: on any test scheme both sides parametrize two sections of $U$ with equal images in $Y$. Equality in $Y$ is equality in its open subfunctor $X$, and equality of their maps to $S$ is equality to $B$. Fibre products are supplied by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U\times_BU$ is affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The hypothesis on $\Delta_{Y/S}$ therefore makes $R$ quasi-compact. The projection $R\to U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since $U$ is affine and quasi-separated. By [lem-sfb-space-qs-atlas-criterion], $X$ is absolutely quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 07S4 (lemma-quasi-separated); affine-base reduction of the relative hypothesis, using the diagonal pullback formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-qc-etale-fibre-bound] to the affine (hence quasi-compact) scheme $U$ and the quasi-separated space $X$. It gives a bound $N$ for geometric fibre cardinalities of $a$. Also $a$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence](1). The affine scheme $U$ is absolutely separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], applied to its structure map. Hence [lem-a1-separated-etale-chart] makes $a$ separated. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-etale-closed-degree-loci] are now satisfied: $D_r=\{x:|U_{\bar x}|\leq r\}$ is closed for every $r\geq0$.

Surjectivity and nonemptiness of $X$ imply that some geometric fibre is nonempty and every fibre is nonempty. The nonempty finite set of attained cardinalities, contained in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, has a largest member $d\geq1$. Thus $T=|X|\setminus D_{d-1}$ is nonempty and open, and every fibre over $T$ has exactly $d$ points. Realize $T$ as an open subspace by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Its pullback $U_T=U\times_XT$ is an open subscheme of $U$ by the definition of open subspace. The morphism $a_T:U_T\to T$ remains surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Its diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal of $a$, so is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

Apply [lem-sfb-space-constant-degree-etale-finite] with degree $d$ to $a_T$. Its source is a scheme, it is quasi-compact separated etale, and its geometric fibres have exactly $d$ points. It is finite locally free on scheme tests. Since $U_T$ is an open subscheme of the affine scheme $U$, [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-open-affine-cover] implies that $T$ is a scheme. It is a nonempty open subspace of $Y$ contained in $O$, so maximality of $V$ gives $T\subseteq V$.

source.place: Tag 03JI (proposition-reasonable-open-dense-scheme), finite locally free maximum-degree piece; spaces-properties.tex Tag 07S6 (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence-global).

proof.text: Therefore every nonempty open $O$ meets $|V|$, which is exactly $\overline{|V|}=|Y|$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] the open immersion $j:V\to Y$ identifies $|V|$ homeomorphically with its open image. The $S$-structure is the composite through $Y$. When $Y$ is empty its largest schematic open is empty and the same density criterion is vacuous; no positive degree is selected in that case.

Each nonempty open O contains an open X with an affine atlas U whose structure map factors through an affine open B of S. Step 2 shows U x_X U -> U x_B U is the scheme test of the relative diagonal (X->Y and B->S are monomorphisms), so R is quasi-compact, and the 07S4 criterion node makes X absolutely quasi-separated (no absolute qs of Y assumed, E1 OK). Step 3 gets the fibre bound N, a quasi-compact and a separated (via U affine, hence separated) and the closed degree loci D_r. Step 4 takes d as the maximum attained degree (d>=1), sets T = |X| minus D_{d-1}, and shows a_T is surjective etale, quasi-compact, and has a closed diagonal by base change. Step 5 gives a_T finite locally free, then 07S6 makes T a scheme, so T lies in V by maximality. Step 6 is the elementary density argument. Every cited statement says what its step uses; proof_deps equals the union of the uses; there is no cycle.
